{"body":"Closes #53.

pi-action now puts the repository's `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) into the system prompt, as pi's coding agent does, so the repository's conventions apply from the first request.

## What changes

- **`src/context-files.ts`**: finds, reads, and limits the context files, and defines the built-in `pi-action-context` extension with its one section, `project_context`. The text has the same shape as pi's `# Project Context` block.
  1. `<agent_dir>/AGENTS.md`, or else `CLAUDE.md`. Only when `agent_dir` is set.
  2. For each directory from the workspace root (`GITHUB_WORKSPACE`) down to `cwd`: `AGENTS.md`, or else `CLAUDE.md`. It never reads above the workspace. If `cwd` is not inside the workspace, `cwd` counts as the root.
  3. Nested files below `cwd` are not loaded. The section names up to 20 of them in one sentence, found with `git ls-files` so that ignored files are left out.
- **Read once per run.** `run.ts` reads the files during setup and passes the text to `Thread.open`. The section returns that fixed text, so an edit to `AGENTS.md` during the run causes no section update and keeps the prompt cache. A later run on the same thread sends the new content as a normal section update.
- **`Thread.open`** installs `pi-action-context` right after `CodingTools` and before the user's extensions, so pit's guidelines come after the repository's rules. With no files, the section is left out. `createDurableExtensions` reserves the name.
- **Inputs**: `context_files` (default `true`, as the issue suggests) and `context_files_max_bytes` (default `65536`). When the files go over the limit, the file at the limit is cut at a character boundary and gets a note for the model. Later files are left out and listed. Both write a log warning.
- **Pull requests from forks** (`isForkPullRequest`): the workspace files are read from `pull_request.base.sha` with `git show`, and the commit is fetched if a shallow clone doesn't have it. If that fails, no workspace files are loaded and a warning says why. The section tells the model the files came from the base commit.
- **Sanitising**: invisible characters are removed (the new `removeInvisibleCharacters()` in `security.ts`, which `sanitizeInput()` now also uses). HTML comments are kept.
- **Log**: the setup group gets a line such as `Context files: AGENTS.md (2.1 KiB)`.

## Docs

`docs/prompts.md` has a new section, *The system prompt*, which is the main reference. `docs/how-it-works.md` (the run steps and commit conventions; it no longer says "pi-action does not add them to the prompt"), `docs/security.md` (a new section, *Context files from the repository*: fork pull requests vs. branches in the same repository), `docs/extensions.md` (install order and reserved names), the README feature list and inputs table, and the CONTRIBUTING source table are also updated.

## Tests

- `src/context-files.test.ts`: the section text; discovery order (agent_dir first, then root down to cwd, `AGENTS.md` before `CLAUDE.md`); agent_dir equal to the root is loaded only once; the workspace boundary; the cut, with its notes and warnings; invisible characters; listing nested files (one per directory, ignored files skipped, cap of 20); fork pull requests (fetching the base commit from a shallow clone, and the base commit missing or invalid).
- `src/thread.test.ts`: `project_context` comes before the extensions' sections. It is left out without files. **No section update** when the agent rewrites `AGENTS.md` during a run.
- `src/run.test.ts`: from start to finish, with the log line in the setup group. `context_files: false` removes the section on the next run. A fork pull request with no base sha.
- Input, default, and reserved-name tests.

`npm run check` passes.

## Release notes

### Added

- pi-action puts `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) into the system prompt, as pi does. This is **on by default**. Turn it off with `context_files: false`. On pull requests from forks, the files come from the base commit. (#53)

Not included: `.pi/SYSTEM.md` / `APPEND_SYSTEM.md`, and skills (#54), which can share the `pi-action-context` extension.","title":"feat: load AGENTS.md into the system prompt"}
{"body":"Closes #54.

pi-action now loads [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) the way pi's coding agent does. Docs: [`docs/skills.md`](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/blob/feat/skills/docs/skills.md).

### Discovery (`src/skills.ts`)
- Searched in this order, and the first skill with a name wins (the others get a warning):
  1. Packages: those in `extensions`, then those in the new optional **`skills`** input (same spec syntax). Each package gives its `pi.skills` list, or else its `skills/` directory. Packages in `skills` are installed but **their code never runs**. A package that has only skills no longer gets the "has no pi extensions" warning.
  2. Project: `.pi/skills/` and `.agents/skills/`, **only with `trust_project: true`**. Without it, the log says `Not loading the skills in .pi/skills: trust_project is off`.
  3. User: `<agent_dir>/skills/`, when `agent_dir` is set.
- Skills are found recursively. A directory with a `SKILL.md` is a skill, and its subdirectories are its resources, not more skills. Hidden directories and `node_modules` are skipped.
- Frontmatter is checked against the Agent Skills rules. `name` is required, uses `a-z0-9` and single inner hyphens, is at most 64 characters, and must match the directory name. `description` is required and at most 1024 characters. A skill that breaks a rule is skipped, and the warning gives the reason. `disable-model-invocation: true` keeps a skill out of the prompt list but still allows `/skill:name`.
- There's no YAML dependency. A small parser handles top-level scalars: plain, quoted, multi-line, and `|`/`>` blocks. Nested maps are ignored.
- Setup log line: `Skills: release (project), deploy (project, /skill:deploy only), changelog (xyz-skills)`.

### Prompt section
- New built-in pi-durable extension `pi-action` (`src/builtin-extension.ts`). It is installed after `coding-tools` and before the user's extensions, so they can `wrapSection("available_skills", …)`. Its name is reserved. #53 can add the AGENTS.md section to it.
- `available_skills` uses the wording from the issue, with absolute locations and XML escaping. The section is left out when no skill is listed.
- The text is memoized per run. When the model sees `typescript` and no `read` tool (pit-only, #52), it says `workspace.read` instead of "the read tool".

### `/skill:<name> args`
- Replaces the task with `<skill name=… location=…>References are relative to <dir>.\n\n<body>\n</skill>\n\n<args>`, as pi does. This works in first messages, follow-ups and `prompt`, but not in answers. It runs before prompt-template expansion.
- An unknown name sets a new `Trigger.rejected`. `ThreadConversation` doesn't submit the trigger. Instead it replies with an error listing the skills, gets the 😕 reaction, and records it as posted so later runs don't post it again.
- The log shows `▶ … /skill:release 2.4.0 (skill from project)`. The comment entry stores `skill` and `typed`.

### Tests
- `src/skills.test.ts`: frontmatter parsing, discovery order and recursion, name collisions, each validation rule, section text and escaping, tool-aware wording, memoization, expansion and rejection.
- `src/extensions.test.ts`: `pi.skills` versus `skills/`, the `skills` input (including npm install and not running code).
- `src/run.test.ts`, end to end: system prompt, first-message and follow-up expansion, the `trust_project` gate, an unknown-skill error reply that isn't posted again.

### Docs
New `docs/skills.md`. Also updated: README (input table, docs table), `docs/extensions.md`, `docs/security.md` ("Skills from the repository"), `docs/prompts.md`, `docs/how-it-works.md` and CONTRIBUTING (source map).

### Known limitation
A run whose only request is an unknown `/skill:` still opens the thread, because `Thread.open` commits. The next request on that issue is then sent as a follow-up without the issue's context. Other runs that fail early on a new thread behave the same way.

`npm run check` passes (439 tests).","title":"feat: load skills (SKILL.md), list them in the system prompt, and expand /skill:<name>"}
{"body":"Closes #65.

## What changed

pi-action now sends pi's base system prompt. Before, the system message had only `project_context`, `available_skills`, and the extensions' sections. The model was not told what it is, which tools it has, pi's rules, or its working directory.

The built-in `pi-action` extension (`src/builtin-extension.ts`) now renders pi 1.5.2's sections (`buildSystemPromptSections`) in pi's order:

1. `preamble`: untagged (`tag: false`), as in pi
2. `tools`: one line for each **offered** tool that has a snippet, then `Additional tools may be available.`, or `(none)`
3. `rules`: pi's `buildRules()`, with duplicates removed. The bash file-operation rule appears only without grep, find, or ls. Then each tool's guidelines, then pi's two general rules
4. `project_context`
5. `available_skills`
6. `cwd`: `input.agent.cwd`, with `/` as the separator
7. then the extensions' sections (pit's)

pi's `docs` section is left out, as the issue asks (pi-action ships no pi docs). APPEND_SYSTEM.md (#67) is not part of this PR.

### Design notes
- **Order.** `project_context` moves from the `pi-action-context` extension into `pi-action`, so that one extension owns pi's whole ordered list. `pi-action-context` is removed, and that name is no longer reserved. `Thread` no longer takes `projectContext`: `run.ts` passes it to `createBuiltinExtension`. The wraps of later extensions still apply. A test wraps `rules`.
- **Tools come from the request.** `tools` and `rules` are rendered from `input.agent.tools`, after `exclude_tools`, `model_tools_hidden`, and the wraps. In a pit-only setup the model sees `- typescript: Execute TypeScript with explicit function dependencies` and only pi's two general rules. pit's guidelines stay in `pit_guidelines` and are not repeated.
- **Snippets and guidelines.** There is a table for `read`, `write`, `edit`, and `bash`, copied from pi-coding-agent 1.5.2's `*ToolSystemPromptContribution`, without bash's `PI_*` line. It also has pit's `PROMPT_SNIPPET` for `typescript`, because pit's durable tool registration has no `promptSnippet`. A tool can set its own `promptSnippet` and `promptGuidelines`. pi-action checks their types before it uses them, and they replace the table entry. `PI_PROMPT_VERSION` has a test that pins it to the installed pi-durable version, so a pi upgrade makes you compare the copied text again.
- **Prompt cache.** Each section is a pure function of the run's fixed tool set and inputs. A test checks that the system message is identical across two requests of one run, including when the agent edits AGENTS.md.
- **Existing threads.** pi-durable's `planSections` sees new keys that come *before* the sections the thread already shows. So it removes and re-adds the sections one time, on the thread's next request. This is the "accept the one remove-and-re-add" option from the issue. It is documented in `docs/prompts.md`.
- No `prompt_template` change.

## Tests
- `src/builtin-extension.test.ts`: the snippet table and a tool's own fields, invalid fields ignored, deduplicated rules, the bash rule with grep, find, or ls, the untagged preamble, cwd backslashes, sections left out, and the version pin.
- `src/thread.test.ts`: the order and exact text of the whole rendered system prompt (`getSystemMessageText`). Also the section text for the default tools, pit-only, `exclude_tools: bash`, no tool with a snippet (`(none)`), unchanged text across two requests, and a `wrapSection("rules")` override.

One case differs from the issue: pi-action refuses a run where the model has no tools at all. So the `(none)` test offers one custom tool that has no snippet.

## Docs
- `docs/prompts.md`: "The system prompt" now lists every section in order, with the default `tools` and `rules` text, the snippet and guideline rules, the prompt cache, and existing threads.
- `docs/extensions.md`: the section keys for `wrapSection`, and the reserved names without `pi-action-context`.
- `docs/how-it-works.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` (the source file table).

`npm run check` passes.","title":"feat: send pi's base system prompt sections (preamble, tools, rules, cwd)"}
